steps.text: In a large pot over medium high heat, saute the mushrooms and leeks in the butter or margarine and olive oil until tender. Add the sherry and reduce liquid by half.
Then add the beef broth, water and ground black pepper. Bring to a boil and add the pasta. Boil gently for 10 minutes, or until the pasta is tender. Garnish with sliced mushrooms if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Mushroom and Leek Soup
raw_recipe.description: Combine mushrooms, leeks, dry sherry, and pasta for this simple and sumptuous soup. A lovely beginning or finish for any meal, and ready to serve in less than 20 minutes.
raw_recipe.name: Mushroom and Leek Soup

review.reviewBody: Quick, easy and absolutely fantastic! I used chicken broth, added more mushrooms and added fresh spinach leaves during the last few minutes. Beautiful and everyone loves it!

I did let it simmer longer, and I think that improved the flavor. We liked it, but next time, I’ll add some chopped carrot which will not only kick up the flavor, but also give it a pop of color improving its eye appeal. Would recommend not skipping the sherry up front, it’s important. Garnished with some chopped parsley, and enjoyed for lunch.

With some substitutions and additions, this is a 5 star recipe! After reading other reviews, I used herb-ox chicken bouillon instead of beef bouillon for the broth, and used white wine instead of sherry. Since I doubled my recipe, I also added additional mushrooms and leeks, to make it a bit more hardy. I used mixed mushrooms instead of just one kind. The last time I made it, I added ground pork cooked in olive oil after I added the chicken broth. I also did what other reviewers did and added spinach at the end. So healthy and yummy! This past time that I made it, with the pork, my hubby said it was the best soup he's ever had. Awesome!

Prior reviews helpful. I used chicken broth, more leeks and mushrooms than recipe. I also added about 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp tarragon for some flavor. Husband said it was "good!" I would make again, but use less oil initially, maybe only 2 tbsp total.

THIS IS OUTSTANDING! Super simple. I was just looking for something to do with my left over leeks from another dish. I just happened to have beef stock in the freezer that I made myself. I did not add orzo. I served this like French Onion Soup (provolone over crunchy bread). I made a boat load so I'm about to freeze the rest for winter. VERY tasty! VERY.

I changed it up a bit with some left over veggies in the fridge . 2 chicken bouillon cubes, baby Bella mushrooms , leeks, 4 whole garlic cloves , shredded Brussel sprouts and a left over tomato, red pepper flakes, orzo , thyme and rosemary, let it all simmer together and it’s PHENOMENAL!! I did not add any additional salt ( can’t have it 😑) and a dash of pepper .

So happy to find a leek soup that doesn't include potatoes! At the end of sauteing the mushrooms and leeks, I added 2 chopped garlic cloves. I also added 2 chopped carrots to the broth and used barley instead of the orzo pasta. Finally, I added some miso at the end of cooking time. Wonderful! Will be making regularly. Thanks for the recipe.

Great recipe! I sautéed onions, mushrooms (12 oz) and a carrot in olive oil and garlic butter, used brandy and half mushroom stock, half beef stock. Excellent flavour - I will definitely make this again.

Like most people I made some changes to this soup. Used homemade chicken broth and a chicken broth cube, no sherry so used brandy, pureed half the leeks and mushrooms first after cooking, didn't add orzo and added fresh parsley. It's a mild soup that would go well with a full flavoured meal. I might add pureed potato or some cream next time.

This was a tasty soup. Very easy to prepare. I would have given it 5 stars, but I had to add salt, garlic and some red hot pepper flakes. I also substitued the 3 3/4 cups of water for 2 cups of chicken stock. The beef/chicken stock flavor was nice. I added about a 1/2 tablespoon of chopped garlic to the leeks and mushrooms while they were cooking. I also added salt to taste and the red pepper to taste. I also used 2 whole leeks and more pasta. I will make this again. Thank you for this simple and elegant soup.

Pretty good... used chicken broth in place of the water, doubled the mushrooms and leeks, used 3/4 cup of orzo, and added about 2 cloves of garlic, a 1/2 tsp of thyme, and a sprinkle of crushed red pepper. I also halved the oil and butter and didn't miss the extra fat! I had a little whole grain garlic bread leftover and I cut it in small pieces and added it in as "croutons"... the same could be done with some wheat toast. Good, refreshing light soup.
Second time making this recipe, it’s easy to follow. Ingredients are in every day, stores or your cabinet, and it cooks up terribly quickly.
Substitute the dry sherry with red vermouth and add some matzarrela cheese at the end once is in the bowl withoven baked bread is a fancy version of French onion soup
This was perfect as is except I used half the oil/butter called for to soften the leek. That doesn't count, right?

Very good with mods. Using all beef broth is too heavy and greasy. I make a double batch with 16 oz mushrooms, about 3-4 giant leeks (3 cups), 12 cups of water with 1/3 rounded cup of chicken better than bouillon + 2Tblsp beef BBB. Quite a few splashes of mushroom soy + 1.5 cups orzo.

I loved the ease of this soup recipe. And it was delicious! I doubled the recipe, used baby bella mushrooms, and used broth from Osem brand powdered chicken flavored consomme instead of beef broth. I didn't have orzo, so substituted stelline, star shaped pasta instead. It hit the spot. Yet...I might add some fresh herbs or other seasonings next time I make it.
Good but a bit bland, and it has too much pepper. I added a tablespoon of Thai chili paste, which added the right flavor.
My family loved this recipe! I did double the mushrooms and used chicken broth instead of beef broth.
Easy and delicious! The only change I made was a little less broth for a little heartier soup. It’s also a pretty quick soup to make.
Very good but a little bland, although might be too much pepper for some. I did exactly as the recipe stated. Next time I would add more sherry and Somme herbs and/or garlic.
